translations.text: "The angel Gabriel was sent," and so on.
Our Almighty Creator, who through his wisdom created all creatures without any pre-existing matter, and through his will gave them life,
created mankind so that through obedience and humility they might earn the heavenly honour that the devil forfeited through pride.
Then the man too was deceived by the devil's tricks, so that he broke his Creator's command, and was handed over to the devil, together with all his offspring, into the torment of hell.
Yet Almighty God took pity on the miseries of all mankind, and considered how he might redeem his handiwork from the devil's power;
Therefore He took pity on the man, because he had been deceived by the devil's cunning arts. But He did not pity the devil's fall at all,
because the devil was not led astray by any instigation; he himself devised the arrogance through which he fell. And therefore the cruel devil remains in perdition for ever and ever.

Then from the beginning of mankind the Almighty God made known, sometimes through signs, sometimes through prophecies, that he would rescue mankind through the one by whom he had made all creatures: through his own Son.
Now these prophecies were set down in many ways in the holy scriptures before the Son of God took on human nature. Some were also prophesied about the blessed Mary.
One of these prophecies is Isaiah's, who wrote among his prophecies, saying: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive in her womb and bear a Son,
and his name shall be called Emmanuel," which is translated in our language as 'God is with us.' Again, the prophet Ezekiel saw in his prophecy a shut gate in the house of God,
and an angel said to him: "This gate shall not be opened to any man; the Lord alone shall go in through that gate and go out again, and it shall be shut for ever."
That closed gate in the house of God signified the holy virginity of the blessed Mary.
The Lord, the Lord of all lords, that is Christ, came into her womb and through her was born in human nature, and that gate shall be shut for ever;
that is, Mary was a virgin before the birth, a virgin in the birth, and a virgin after the birth.
The prophecies about Christ's birth and about the blessed Mary's virginity are set down in many ways in the Old Law, and whoever wishes to study them will find them there in great abundance.
The apostle Paul also said, "When the fullness of time came, God the Father sent his Son for the redemption of mankind."
That glorious mission was fulfilled on this day, as Christ's book tells us, saying: "God's archangel Gabriel was sent from God to the Galilean town of Nazareth,
to the virgin who was called Mary, and she was descended from the family of David, the great king, and she was betrothed to the righteous Joseph," and so on.
In today's reading we have heard the beginning of our redemption, through which we cast off the harmful old state, and we are counted among God's children through Christ's incarnation.
It was a very fitting beginning of human redemption that the angel was sent from God to the virgin to announce God's birth through her,
because the first cause of human ruin was when the devil sent another devil, in the likeness of a serpent, to the first-created woman, Eve, to deceive her.
Death and ruin came to us then through a woman, and life and salvation came to us again through a woman.

The archangel who announced the Saviour's birth was called Gabriel, which is translated 'God's strength.' He announced the coming of the one whom the psalmist praised with these words: "The Lord is strong and mighty in battle."
In that battle, without doubt, in which the Saviour overcame the devil and snatched the world away from him.
"Mary was betrothed to Joseph the righteous." Why did God wish to be born of a betrothed maiden? For a great reason, and also out of necessity.
The Jewish people kept God's law at that time: the law taught that every woman who had a child outside lawful marriage should be stoned.
Now then, if Mary had been unbetrothed and had a child, the Jewish people would have stoned her to death according to God's law.
So, through God's providence, she was betrothed to the righteous man, and everyone supposed that he was the child's father, but he was not.
But when Joseph perceived that Mary was with child, he became sad and would not come near her, and thought that he would put her away secretly.

While Joseph was pondering this, God's angel came to him and commanded him that he should take care of both the mother and the child, and said that the child had not been begotten by any man, but was of the Holy Spirit.
Yet the Holy Spirit is not Christ's Father, but he is named in connection with the bringing about of Christ's humanity, because he is the Will and the Love of the Father and of the Son.
Now the humanity was brought about through that great Will, and yet it is the indivisible work of all Three of them.
They are three in persons, Father, and Son, and Holy Spirit, and one indivisible God in one Godhead.
Then Joseph, as the angel had commanded him, took care of both Mary and the child, and was her witness that she was a virgin,
and he was Christ's foster-father, and served him in his human nature with his help and comfort in all things.
The angel greeted Mary and said that she was filled with God's grace, and that God was with her, and that she was blessed among women.
Truly she was filled with God's grace, because it was granted to her that she should bear the one who established all graces and all truths.
God was with her because he was enclosed in her womb, he who encloses the whole world in his one hand.
And she was blessed among women because, without precedent among women, with the beauty of her maidenhood, she was the mother of the Almighty God.
The angel encouraged her with his words and said to her, "Behold, you shall conceive in your womb, and you shall bear a son."
Recognize now, through these words, a true man born of a virgin body.
His name was Jesus, that is, Saviour, because he saves all those who rightly believe in him. "He shall be great, and he shall be called Son of the Most High."
Believe now, through these words, that he is true God of true God, and co-eternal with his Father, of whom he was eternally begotten without beginning.

Christ held David's throne, not bodily but spiritually, because he is King of all kings, and reigns over his chosen people, both over the people of Israel and over all other nations who abide in the right faith;
and Christ will bring them all to his eternal kingdom. Israel means 'seeing God,' and Jacob means 'Supplanter.'
Now those people who see God with their minds through faith, and those who supplant sins, belong to God's kingdom, which never fails.
Then Mary said to the angel, "How can it be that I should have a child, since I have no knowledge of any man?
I resolved to end my life in virginity: how then can it come about that I should give birth without union with a man?"
Then the angel answered the maiden, "The Holy Spirit will come upon you from above, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you." Through the working of the Holy Spirit,
as we said before, Christ was conceived in human nature; and Mary his mother was overshadowed through the power of the Holy Spirit. How was she overshadowed?
She was so overshadowed that she was cleansed and shielded against all sins through the power of the Holy Spirit, and filled and sanctified with heavenly gifts.
The angel said, "The Holy One who will be born of you will be called the Son of God."
Truly all people are conceived in unrighteousness and born in sins, as the prophet said. But our Savior alone was conceived without unrighteousness and born without sins.
and he was holy at once, as soon as he was man, and perfect God, the Son of Almighty God, man and God in one person.
Then Mary said to the angel, "I am God's handmaid; let it happen to me according to your word." Great humility dwelt in her mind when she spoke these words.
She did not say, "I am God's mother," or, "I am queen of the whole world," but said, "I am God's handmaid."
This is as holy scripture admonishes us, saying, "The greater you are, the more you should humble yourself in all things, and you will find grace and reward with God."
She said to the angel, "Let it happen to me according to your word": that is, Let it be as you say, that the Son of Almighty God may come into my womb,
and take human substance from me, and come forth from me for the redemption of the world, as a bridegroom from his bridal bed.
So our Saviour came into Mary's womb on this day, which is called Annuntiatio Sanctae Mariae, that is, the Day of Mary's Annunciation;
On that day the archangel Gabriel announced to the pure virgin that God would come to mankind through her. She believed the angel's message, and so through faith she received God into her womb.

and she carried him until the feast-day of Midwinter (Christmas), and then gave birth to him in true human nature, he who was always dwelling in the Godhead with his Father and with the Holy Spirit, the three of them one indivisible God.
Now the evangelist says that Mary, after the angel's announcement, went to her kinswoman Elizabeth, who was the wife of Zechariah.
They were both righteous, and kept God's commandments blamelessly. They were without a child until they were worn out with age.
Then the same angel Gabriel came to Zechariah six months before he came to Mary, and announced that he would have a son by his old wife, John the Baptist.
But he did not believe the angel's message. Then the angel said to him, "Since you will not believe my words, be mute until the child is born."
And then he was struck dumb for that whole time because of his unbelief. "Now the blessed Mary came to his house and greeted his wife, her kinswoman Elizabeth.
As soon as the woman heard the virgin's greeting, the child John rejoiced in his mother's womb, and the mother was filled with the Holy Spirit.
and she cried out to Mary in a loud voice and said, "You are blessed among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb. How has it happened to me that the mother of my Lord should come to me?"
"As soon as the sound of your greeting rang in my ears, my child rejoiced in my womb and leapt toward his Lord, whom you carry in your womb."
The child could not yet greet his Savior with words, but he greeted him with a rejoicing spirit.
She said, "Blessed are you, Mary, because you believed the words that were announced to you from God, and it will be accomplished just as it was made known to you."
Then Mary at once sang the hymn of praise that we sing in God's church at every evensong, "Magnificat anima mea Dominum," and so on to the end.
That is, "My soul magnifies the Lord," and so on. It would take a long time for us to expound this whole hymn, but we will briefly run over its most obscure words.
"God has cast down the mighty from their seat": these are the proud, who exalt themselves beyond their due measure.
"And he has raised up the humble"; as Christ himself said in his gospel, "Everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted."
"God fills the hungry with his good things"; as he himself said, "Blessed are those who hunger and long for righteousness, for they shall be filled with righteousness."
"He has sent the rich away empty." The rich here are those who, in their pride, love earthly wealth more than heavenly wealth.
Many rich people thrive before God, those who do as it is written: "The rich man's wealth is the redemption of his soul."
His wealth is the redemption of his soul if, with these passing riches, he buys for himself eternal life and heavenly wealth with God.
If he neglects this and sets his hope on earthly wealth, then God sends him away empty and void of the eternal good things.
"God has received his servant Israel." By that name are signified all those who obey God with true humility, whom he receives into his company.
"As he spoke to our fathers, to Abraham and his offspring for ever." God promised the patriarch Abraham that in his kindred all mankind should be blessed.
The blessed Mary sprang from the line of Abraham, and from Mary came Christ in his human nature, and through Christ all the faithful are blessed.
We are not of Abraham's line in the flesh, but spiritually, as the apostle Paul said, "Truly, if you are Christians, then you are Abraham's offspring, and heirs according to the promise."
The last words of this canticle are "for ever," because our promise, which God promised us, endures for ever and ever without end.

Let us now pray to the blessed and happy maiden Mary that she intercede for us with her own Son and her Creator, the Saviour Christ, who rules all things with the Father and with the Holy Spirit, for ever into eternity. Amen.
